note: Pathogenic dominant de novo RNU2-2 variants were directly reported in 4 of 672 (0.6%) patients with DEEs of unknown cause, directly within the hypothesized 0.5-2.0% range.

evidence.text: In a cohort of patients with developmental and epileptic encephalopathies of unknown cause, recurrent pathogenic RNU2-2 variants were identified in 4 of 672 (0.6%) individuals.

source.title: Pathogenic Variants in RNU2‐2, a Non‐coding Spliceosomal RNA, Cause a Distinctive Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy
source.quote: We identified recurrent pathogenic RNU2-2 variants in 4 of 672 (0.6%) patients with developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs) of unknown cause.

numbers.metric: diagnostic yield in unsolved DEE cohort

evidence.text: Systematic evaluation of 34,329 individuals identified recurrent dominant pathogenic RNU2-2 variants (35 individuals) alongside recessive forms, showing RNU2-2 is a major contributor to NDD/DEE cohorts, nearly as prevalent as ReNU syndrome.

source.title: Systematic analysis of snRNA genes reveals frequent RNU2-2 variants in dominant and recessive developmental and epileptic encephalopathies
authors: C de Vanssay de Blavous Legendre
source.quote: We report RNU2-2 variants in 141 individuals, including 35 with recurrent dominant pathogenic variants and 91 affected members from 73 families with biallelic variants.
